Select the Optimal Biological Dose of gBOIN-ET Trials

Source: R/gboin_et_select_obd.R
gboin_et_select_obd.Rd

Select the optimal biological dose (OBD) from the final data of one or more trials of the gBOIN-ET design: the patients and the total normalized toxicity and efficacy scores at every dose.

Usage

gboin_et_select_obd(
  n_pts,
  n_tox,
  n_resp,
  target,
  target_resp,
  p_saf = NULL,
  p_tox = NULL,
  p_saf_resp = NULL,
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  cutoff_eli_resp = 0.99,
  p_eli = NULL,
  p_eli_resp = NULL,
  est_method = c("observed", "fp_linear", "fp_logistic"),
  obd_method = c("max_resp", "utility_weighted", "utility_truncated_linear",
    "utility_scoring"),
  min_obd_sample = 1,
  w1 = 0.33,
  w2 = 1.09,
  t_low = NULL,
  t_upp = NULL,
  e_low = NULL,
  e_upp = NULL,
  psi00 = 40,
  psi11 = 60,
  early_stop = NULL,
  boinet_compatible = FALSE
)

Arguments

n_pts

Integer vector of patients treated at each dose, or a matrix with one row per trial.

n_tox

Numeric vector or matrix of the same shape as n_pts. Total of the normalized toxicity scores of the patients at each dose.

n_resp

Numeric vector or matrix of the same shape as n_pts. Total of the normalized efficacy scores of the patients at each dose.

target

Numeric scalar. Target DLT probability, for example 0.30.

target_resp

Numeric scalar. Target response probability, for example 0.60.

p_saf

Numeric scalar. Highest DLT probability deemed subtherapeutic. Defaults to 0.1 * target, the value recommended by Takeda et al. (2018), which is far below the 0.6 * target of the BOIN design.

p_tox

Numeric scalar. Lowest DLT probability deemed overly toxic. Defaults to 1.4 * target.

p_saf_resp

Numeric scalar. Highest response probability deemed subtherapeutic. Defaults to 0.6 * target_resp.

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. A dose is no longer admissible when the posterior probability that its DLT rate is below p_eli falls below 1 - cutoff_eli. Defaults to 0.95.

cutoff_eli_resp

Numeric scalar. A dose is no longer admissible when the posterior probability that its response rate is above p_eli_resp falls below 1 - cutoff_eli_resp. Defaults to 0.99.

p_eli

Numeric scalar or NULL. DLT probability of the rule above. Defaults to NULL, which uses target as the 'boinet' package does. Takeda et al. (2018) used 0.40 with a cutoff of 0.90.

p_eli_resp

Numeric scalar or NULL. Response probability of the rule above. Defaults to NULL, which uses p_saf_resp as the 'boinet' package does. Takeda et al. (2018) used 0.20 with a cutoff of 0.90.

est_method

Character scalar. Estimator of the mean efficacy scores: "observed" (the default) for the observed means, "fp_linear" for the linear fractional polynomial of Takeda et al. (2022), or "fp_logistic" for the fractional polynomial logistic regression of the 'boinet' package, which needs the 'mfp' package.

obd_method

Character scalar. Selection rule: "max_resp" (the default) for the admissible dose with the highest estimated response rate up to the estimated MTD, or the dose that maximizes the utility "utility_weighted", "utility_truncated_linear" or "utility_scoring" among the admissible doses.

min_obd_sample

Integer scalar. Only doses given to at least this many patients can be selected. Defaults to 1. The simulations of Takeda et al. (2022) use 6.

w1, w2

Numeric scalars. Weights of the weighted utility q - w1 * p - w2 * p * (p > p_tox), where p and q are the estimated DLT and response rates. Default to 0.33 and 1.09.

t_low, t_upp

Numeric scalars or NULL. DLT rates between which the truncated linear utility falls from one to zero. Default to p_saf and p_tox.

e_low, e_upp

Numeric scalars or NULL. Response rates between which the truncated linear utility rises from zero to one. Default to p_saf_resp / 2 and target_resp.

psi00, psi11

Numeric scalars. Scores of the scoring utility for a patient with neither DLT nor response and for a patient with both, the scores of a response without DLT and of a DLT without response being 100 and 0. Default to 40 and 60.

early_stop

Logical vector or NULL. TRUE for the trials stopped early, which select no OBD. Defaults to NULL, no early stop.

boinet_compatible

Logical scalar. Apply the rules of the 'boinet' package (version 1.6.0) exactly, in which a dose excluded by its DLT data does not exclude the doses above it. Defaults to FALSE; see Details.

Value

A list with components

obd

Integer vector of the selected dose levels, NA when no dose is selected.

reason

Character vector: "selected", "early_stop" or "no_admissible_dose".

probe

Numeric matrix of the estimates of the mean efficacy scores, NA for the doses not tried.

Details

The rules are those of boin_et_select_obd with the mean scores in the place of the observed rates. A dose is admissible when the posterior probability that its mean toxicity score is below p_eli is at least 1 - cutoff_eli, the posterior probability that its mean efficacy score is above p_eli_resp is at least 1 - cutoff_eli_resp, and no lower dose is excluded by its toxicity data. The mean toxicity scores of the doses tried are estimated by isotonic regression with equal weights. Under "max_resp" the estimated MTD is the highest dose whose estimate is as close to target as that of the closest admissible dose, and the OBD is the admissible dose up to the MTD with the highest estimated efficacy score; ties go to the lowest dose. A dose with fewer than min_obd_sample patients takes part in finding the MTD but cannot be selected; when no dose can be selected the reason is "no_admissible_dose".

The estimated efficacy scores (under "max_resp") and the utilities are compared after rounding to ten decimals, and ties go to the lowest dose. Doses whose scores or utilities are equal as fractions then tie whatever the rounding error of the platform; this happens regularly with "utility_scoring", whose default scores give different doses the same utility. boin_et_select_obd follows 'boinet' and compares the unrounded values, so that for whole numbers of DLTs and responses the two functions select the same dose under "max_resp" and can differ in such ties under a utility. The estimates in probe are rounded to ten decimals.

est_method = "fp_linear" fits, by least squares to the scores of the patients, the 36 models b0 + b1 * dose^p1 + b2 * dose^p2 with the powers -2, -1, -0.5, 0 (the logarithm), 0.5, 1, 2 and 3, where a repeated power p stands for dose^p and dose^p * log(dose) and the doses are the dose levels 1, 2 and so on, and takes the fitted values of the model with the smallest residual sum of squares. This is the estimator of Section 2.3 of Takeda et al. (2022), as their program computes it (a normal model with identity link). With three doses or fewer every model passes through the observed means, which are then used. The fit runs in C++.

The program of Takeda et al. (2022) differs from this function in two further points that min_obd_sample = 6 and boinet_compatible = TRUE bring close: it selects only among doses with at least six patients, and it excludes no dose at the end of the trial.

References

Takeda, K., Morita, S. and Taguri, M. (2022). gBOIN-ET: The generalized Bayesian optimal interval design for optimal dose-finding accounting for ordinal graded efficacy and toxicity in early clinical trials. Biometrical Journal, 64(7), 1178-1191. doi:10.1002/bimj.202100263

See also

sim_gboin_et, gboin_et_simulate, boin_et_select_obd

Examples

# One trial: patients and total normalized scores at four doses
gboin_et_select_obd(
  n_pts = c(3, 6, 12, 9), n_tox = c(0, 1, 3.5, 4),
  n_resp = c(0.5, 2, 8, 6.5),
  target = 0.47 / 1.5, target_resp = 0.95 / 1.5
)
#> $obd
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $reason
#> [1] "selected"
#> 
#> $probe
#>            DL1       DL2       DL3       DL4
#> [1,] 0.1666667 0.3333333 0.6666667 0.7222222
#> 

# The efficacy scores estimated by the linear fractional polynomial
gboin_et_select_obd(
  n_pts = c(3, 6, 12, 9), n_tox = c(0, 1, 3.5, 4),
  n_resp = c(0.5, 2, 8, 6.5),
  target = 0.47 / 1.5, target_resp = 0.95 / 1.5, est_method = "fp_linear"
)$probe
#>            DL1       DL2       DL3       DL4
#> [1,] 0.1290505 0.3691855 0.6555476 0.7256849
